title: Where File Type Control sits in the inspection order
aliases: file too large file type control

prose.label: Does the traffic reach it?
prose.text: File Type Control needs decrypted HTTPS, like DLP and Sandbox; see [[zia.ssl-inspection.bypass-impact:dependent-features]]. For FTP, File Type Control applies to the extracted files: [[zia.ftp-control.scope:dlp-sandbox-ftc-on-extracted]].

prose.label: Where is it in the order?
prose.text: {{post-and-response-position}} The DLP side, including the example of a File Type Control block that keeps DLP from firing, is in [[zia.dlp.evaluation:earlier-block-skips-dlp]].

prose.label: Is the file too large?
prose.text: {{rule-count-limit}} {{scan-limit-400mb}} {{limit-equals-size-field-max}} What the service does with files above the limit is open {{gap:over-limit-handling}}. Sandbox's own size handling is in [[zia.sandbox.coverage]]. Where archive extraction happens relative to DLP is open {{gap:archive-extraction-and-dlp-handoff}}.

checks.do: Whether a File Type Control rule is a Block, since a block means no DLP incident for that file.
Whether a file above the 400 MB limit is handled as the tenant expects, since the service's handling is open.

post-and-response-position.statement: For an HTTP POST request, File Type Control checks the POST after Malware Protection and before Data Loss Prevention. For a GET or POST response, it checks the files in the response after Malware Protection and before the Sandbox analysis of unknown files.

quotes: Malware Protection: The Public Service Edge checks files in the request against anti-virus and anti-spyware signatures.
File Type Control: The Public Service Edge checks if the POST request violates your File Type Control policy.
Data Loss Prevention: The Public Service Edge checks if the POST request includes content that violates your organization's DLP policy.
File Type Control: The Public Service Edge checks if any files in the response violate your File Type Control policy.
Sandbox (check for unknown files): If a file in the response has not been previously identified as a malicious file by the Sandbox engine
Malware Protection: The Public Service Edge checks the files in the response against anti-virus and anti-spyware signatures.

evidence.after: This is a user request to submit or post data to the web
This is data sent from the destination host back to the user in response to an HTTP GET

scan-limit-400mb.statement: File scanning has a 400 MB file size limit, and the File Type Control Policy File Size entry in the ZIA limits table is also 400 MB.

quotes: There is a 400MB file size limitation for file scanning.
| File Type Control Policy File Size | 400 MB |

rule-count-limit.statement: The ZIA limits table allows 2,048 File Type Control Policy rules.

limit-equals-size-field-max.statement: 409,600 KB, the largest value the Minimum and Maximum File Size criteria accept, is 400 MB, so the per-rule size bounds can express the whole range up to the scanning limit and no further.
limit-equals-size-field-max.conditions: Arithmetic only: 409,600 KB / 1,024 = 400 MB. The vendor does not state that the two numbers are the same limit.

over-limit-handling.title: What happens to files above 400 MB
over-limit-handling.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Files larger than 400 MB are passed through without inspection - the tenant-level decision on how to treat them falls to the Unscannable Files policy or to the default-rule behavior.' The vendor names excessive size as one reason a file is unscannable (see zia.file-type-control.criteria:unscannable), which suggests an Unscannable Files rule may catch over-limit files, but no source says over-limit files are passed through or that 400 MB is the 'excessive size' threshold. Related: zia.sandbox.coverage:out-of-scope-not-analyzed says over-size files are handled by File Type Control. Resolves with a lab test of a file just over 400 MB against an unscannable-only rule.
over-limit-handling.blocks: advising whether a large download is blocked, allowed or skipped

archive-extraction-and-dlp-handoff.title: Archive extraction at File Type Control and the DLP handoff
archive-extraction-and-dlp-handoff.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Archive extraction happens at FTC. DLP gets the extracted file list downstream - so a ZIP bomb or deeply nested archive can be terminated at FTC without stressing DLP.' The vendor says the service scans archive formats to recognize inner file types; it does not say where extraction happens or that DLP reuses the result. Resolves with a vendor statement or a lab test.
archive-extraction-and-dlp-handoff.blocks: advising where nested archives are stopped
